scores.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, no floats. Append-only double-entry ledger: a DB trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE.
scores.rationale: Correct on money, RLS, idempotency, SAQ A and Connect; small errors are per-tenant KMS keys not enabling per-customer crypto-shredding and no mention of provider idempotency-key expiry.

scores.evidence: Each tenant is the merchant of record and charges through its own payment provider account, so we never hold funds.
scores.rationale: Interprets the ambiguity well and defers scope explicitly, but entitlements, pause/trial semantics and dunning policy details are thin.

scores.evidence: Ledger, invoices and payments are consistent first... Usage ingest is available first: accept to a durable log, dedupe by idempotency key
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, consistency choices and data ownership are applied consistently across phases; only minor loose ends.

scores.evidence: 0 duplicate charges and 0 unreconciled payments over ≥ 10,000 attempts with ≥ 20% fault injection.
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, run early, and continues in production via hourly ledger checks and daily reconciliation, but several thresholds (1M sequences, 150 cases, 10,000 attempts) are unjustified.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: needs projected tenants × peak events/s from the product owner, before Phase 3
scores.rationale: Assumptions and unknowns are labeled, ranked, tied to phases and to what changes if wrong (including the alternative product interpretations).

scores.evidence: a state machine that tolerates "charge status unknown"
scores.rationale: Covers duplicate charges, webhook reordering, worker crash, tax outage, tenant leaks and PAN leakage with detection and mitigation; dunning, late usage events and entitlement outages are weak.

scores.evidence: GitHub Actions builds a signed image and deploys blue/green to ECS. Migrations are expand-only.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, migrations, meaningful alerts, DR drills and kill switches are concrete and sized to a team of 8, though incident ownership and on-call are only lightly described.

scores.evidence: Per-invoice unit cost | — | UNKNOWN: needs our pricing from the product owner, before Phase 7
scores.rationale: Cost drivers (tax API, platform fees, infra, email) and a cost-metering check are named with controls like batching tax calls, but there are no estimates, build-effort costs or growth analysis.

scores.evidence: R3: tenant ID in every row and key, and data cannot be split cleanly later
scores.rationale: Explicit reversibility rating per decision, early validation of the one-way choices, isolation seams (home_cell, TaxProvider) and revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: 2 deployables (core, ingest) plus managed Postgres, a managed queue... no self-hosted Kafka
scores.rationale: Modular monolith with Postgres and deferred columnar store is proportionate; the heavy process (11 validations, SOC2 prep, cell seam, pentest) adds some overhead.

scores.evidence: The request above succeeds with one trace across every tier. One deploy and one rollback both succeed through the pipeline.
scores.rationale: A concrete Phase 0 slice, dependency-justified phase ordering, checkable exit criteria and stated fallbacks on failure make it startable immediately.

checklist.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, no floats... Documented rounding per line.
Finalized invoices are immutable; corrections go through credit notes.
`Idempotency-Key` required on every POST... Webhook ingestion with dedupe and out-of-order handling.
No card numbers ever: only the provider's hosted fields and tokens.
Row-level security (RLS) enforced by an app role without `BYPASSRLS`.
`POST /usage` → durable log → dedupe → hourly aggregates in partitioned Postgres tables.
Subscription lifecycle with upgrades, downgrades and proration.
Tax-ID capture and validation (VIES for EU).
Daily reconciliation of the ledger against Stripe balance transactions, alerting on any difference.
Build the billing core (it is the product). Buy the payment provider (Stripe Connect), tax engine

traps.evidence: Integer minor units plus ISO 4217 currency, no floats.
a DB trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE. Finalized invoices are immutable; corrections go through credit notes.
No card numbers ever: only the provider's hosted fields and tokens.
a CI lint that fails any table without `tenant_id`, `mode` and RLS.

note: A rigorous, well-sequenced plan that is strong on money correctness, isolation, idempotency and assumptions. It is weak on entitlements, dunning policy, subscription-lifecycle detail, late-usage cutoffs and cost quantification.
